newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria currency board needs adequate budget - IMF.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria currency board needs adequate budget - IMF.

text.p: Bulgaria's 1997 budget needs further adjustments to meet requirements of a restrictive fixed exchange rate regime aimed at stabilising the economy, the International Monetary Fund said on Tuesday.

"The important thing is to ensure that the macroeconomic policies are consistent with the currency board and that is why we spend a lot of time on the budget to ensure that there will no need for lending from the central bank to the budget," said IMF team leader Anne McGuirk.
"There is still some work on the budget to be done and we hope we can wind up by Friday," McGuirk told reporters.

Under a $657 million reform and funding agreement with the Fund, Bulgaria pledged to introduce in July a currency board, known as a self-regulating monetary mechanism, where the amount of money in circulation is matched by the amount of foreign exchange reserves.
Under the system the central bank is banned from lending to the government and commercial banks.
The IMF mission arrived two weeks ago to help prepare legal amendments needed to make the system operational.

This year's budget is assumed at a lev/dollar exchange rate of 1,600 or 1,000 levs to the German mark, said Finance Minister Muravei Radev. He declined to give further details before the IMF mission completes its work in Friday.
The anchor currency and rate at which it will be fixed will be decided by parliament and announced few days before the currency board system is introduced.
The new reformist government, which took office last week, said the system will be introduced on July 1 and proposed the German mark as anchor currency in the system.

Bulgaria's parliament passed last week a draft bill that amends central bank functions to accommodate the currency board system on a preliminary first reading. Parliament is expected to debate and pass the amendments on second, final reading next week.

The assembly has yet to debate and approve amendments to the Banking Law, appoint a new central bank management and a head of its issue department which will play key role in the currency board system.
The IMF will consider disbursing a second tranche of the standby arrangement after the currency board system is in place and Bulgaria has met the reform targets for the first review, said McGuirk.
The IMF disbursed in April some $147 million to back grain import costs plus a $32 million first tranche for balance of payments support.
